title: Jamming with the waffle man's bugle
summary: The waffle man used a bugle to advertise his wagon; young George played along and learned tunes from him by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what's the waffle man?

He was a guy that had a stove and a wagon and he had his wagon made into, like a kitchen and he used to drive around all day selling hot waffles and he'd make the, had the waffle iron and those things in his wagon and the coal fired and then people would buy that, say for five cents they'd get maybe six waffles.
Yeah, five cents for six waffles.
Yeah.
Yeah, not bad. But what was his bugle for?
Just an attraction, just an attraction. Yeah. He was an advertisement. People would blow, you know, blow the bugle. They knew the sound of the bugle. They knew he was nearby.
And so you would go out and play with the waffle guy? Yeah. With the waffle man?
Yes.
Yeah, that's great. You were the waffle man. Did he like seeing you?
Oh, we had a ball.
Yeah?
Yes, he liked to play with me and I learned a lot from him also.
Really?
Yes, I did. What did you learn
from the waffle man?

Well, tunes that he would play that I would pick him up by ear and then I would practice them. Next time, he'd come around, maybe it might have been two weeks, maybe a month, I'd have that tuned on so we would jam on that tune.
What tune? Like,

what tunes did the waffle man play? Well, like one of them, I said, like the, I remember, I ain't gonna run around no more and then we'd play, like we'd take certain parts in the key of, say, B flat, which used to be a key of C for maybe a B flat bugle and anything that was near that in that key of C for the bugle, we'd kind of jam if it's no more than four medges on it, you know. We'd jam right on the four medges or the eight medges, whatever, it would go in without the chains, too many changes and we'd just stay right in there and blow.
When you say jam, you mean just improvising?
Yes.
